extracted.intended_audience: poets, essayists, literary critics, and newspaper editors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for composing extended poems, literary essays, and conducting a newspaper — covering subject-unity and descriptive practice, prose style, moral framing of political questions, historical method, and editorial impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of subject in a long poem
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek a subject that gives equal room and freedom for description, incident, and impassioned reflections on men, nature, and society, yet supplies in itself a natural connection to the parts, and unity to the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example offered: trace a stream from its source to the sea so the stages (source, bank, cottage, hamlet, market-town, seaport) provide a continuing natural link; this avoids the defect of a titular subject that disappears after a few pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid awkward connections and abrupt transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The poem should not have frequently awkward connections, and transitions must not be abrupt and arbitrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique given of The Task: its title-subject is not carried beyond the first pages, producing disjointed parts. Ensure the leading subject informs and connects successive sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compose from direct observation and scene-studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Make studies on location and often mould thoughts into verse with the objects and imagery immediately before the senses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical method: walk the landscape (e.g., Quantock), carry pencil and memorandum-book, make 'studies' and convert immediate sensory impressions into poetry; favors accuracy of detail and vitality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose style: clarity, concision, and avoidance of excessive refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid disproportionate demand on the reader's attention: do not indulge excess refinement, unnecessary beating of the ground, length and laborious construction of periods, obscurity, or a love of paradox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance effortful intellectual rigor with readability; the author defends long labor behind ideas but recognizes that style should not needlessly obscure or over-elaborate what could be said more plainly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and honest intellectual labour
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not 'trick out in other words the thoughts of others' or present recycled claims as one's own; substantive original investigation and labour are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author asserts that he spent months on acquisitions otherwise represented in a day; the implied standard rewards deep investigation and penalizes mere rephrasing or opportunistic summarizing of others' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper/editorial conduct on fixed and announced principles
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper should be conducted on certain fixed and announced principles, and the editor should not be obliged or requested to deviate from them in favour of any party or event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impartiality defined as 'an honest and enlightened adherence to a code of intelligible principles previously announced, and faithfully referred to in support of every judgment on men and events.' Promises consistency and transparency to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pandering, partisan flattery, or commercial sycophancy
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor must avoid indulging malign passion or seeking to make money by flattering the envy and cupidity, vindictive resentfulness and self-conceit of the half-nitted vulgar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejects both indiscriminate abuse and calculated pandering to popular prejudices for profit; editorial tone should resist mob-sycophancy and malicious partisanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place public questions and events in a moral point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism and journalism should place questions and events of the day in a moral point of view: trace policies to permanent principles and give principles interest by applying them to particular measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice gives dignity to measures and interest to principles; it also aids readers' moral evaluation rather than mere partisan reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic precision in political terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish and define political terms (e.g., Jacobin, republican, democrat, demagogue) carefully so words cease being mere terms of abuse and become analytic tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author claims merit for having defined 'Jacobinism' and distinguishing it from related but distinct phenomena, thus rescuing language from rhetorical misuse and clarifying public debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical method for judging and predicting political events
rubrics_metrics.description: When comparing present events to the past, procure contemporary historians, memorialists, and pamphleteers; subtract points of difference from likeness and conjecture future results from the remaining resemblance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use original documents and authentic accounts of the present, apply a philosophic tact for what is truly important in facts; this produces more reliable judgments about probable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion of a scholar's utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure a scholar's usefulness by the number and moral value of the truths he has been the means of throwing into general circulation, and by the number and value of minds he has excited into activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication count alone is an insufficient metric; consider influence on readers, pupils, and the diffusion of valuable ideas as the true test of intellectual usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faith and religion: moral origin and limits of purely intellectual proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Religion must have a moral origin; its evidence cannot be wholly independent of the will, and arguments purely of the understanding may be neutral or inconclusive regarding revealed religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the intellect cannot definitively disprove faith, moral feeling, conscience, analogy of experience, and practical necessities play essential roles; making religion intellectually demonstrable risks undermining the moral efficacy of faith.
